Applying A6's content test against the WEB bytes I measure five substantive qualifying runs: P06-010 'for I have spoken it' (5 words, WEB 28:10, straight-quoted, NO in-field web: reference); P06-011 'you have become a terror, and' (6 words, WEB 28:19, straight-quoted, NO in-field web: reference); P06-012 'know that I am the Lord' (6 words, WEB 28:24, straight-quoted, NO in-field web: reference); P06-009 'take up a lamentation [Hebrew] over Tyre' (6 words, WEB 27:2, straight-quoted, web: reference PRESENT - delimiter half only); P06-011 'son of man, take up a lamentation [Hebrew] over the king of Tyre' (12 words, WEB 28:12, straight-quoted, web: reference PRESENT - delimiter half only). Seven other runs of 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20 and 44 words are correctly curly-quoted with in-field web: references, so the authors knew the convention; what the member misses is the gloss-shaped run. Three further literal hits are incidental collocations and one is an artifact of my own tokeniser, and I report those separately rather than inflating the count.
the_four_validator_members_answered.universals: Attributed count 43. Answered individually: 15 genuine, 28 false positives. The 15 collapse to 9 distinct objects because the member fires repeatedly on one sentence. The 28 false positives cluster in three formulae the rulings expressly sanction - A3's count-only paseq disclosure, A1's Qere note-layer discipline, and A16's one-strongest-rejected-alternative wording - so the member is largely firing on compliance. My test: identify the exact absolute or exclusive proposition, measure its truth against the OSHB bytes or a pinned artifact, then ask whether a seam or a rejection rests on it, which is A5's own grading axis. Earlier peers report 0 of 50 and 15 of 62; my 15 of 43 is close to the second, and I did not assume either rate. Separately MEASURED: on 5 of the 43 flags the flag's own context window does not contain its claim string, and on one of those five - P06-012, the genuine flag on that row - a reviewer working from the context alone would clear it.
the_four_validator_members_answered.refs_mirror: Attributed count 10. Wrong in BOTH directions at once. (a) All ten are per-row FALSE POSITIVES, because MEASURED the in-window content of every flag is nothing but the two far-side seam verses, and A4's own last sentence says not to file per-row findings for the far-side verse. (b) The member simultaneously MISSES eight in-window prose-argued verses on four rows that the A4 rule does reach: MT 27:11, 27:12, 27:25, 27:26 (P06-009's two candidate interior cuts); MT 28:5, 28:7, 28:9 (P06-010's interior samekh and the two verses its rejected classification turns on); MT 29:6 (P07-001's own rejected close). The mechanism: A4's window is [first-1, last+1] and therefore CONTAINS the span, while the scoping file's split treats 'in window' as the two adjacent verses only and buckets every in-span argued verse as outside. That is a testable candidate explanation for the scoping file's own unresolved 111-verse discrepancy, offered as a hypothesis and not as a correction to the controlling agent's 708/240 measurement. On one row, P07-009, the rule finds a hit where the member found none, which also shows the builder's range expansion is inconsistent across rows.
the_four_validator_members_answered.mark_symmetry: Attributed count 0. TRUE NEGATIVE, independently confirmed. I ran the MARKS-3D three-direction audit on all eleven rows against pmarks_Ezek.json at its pinned digest - onset-seam mark on the verse before the first, interior marks on first through last-but-one, close-seam mark on the last verse, with the C1 direction convention as the mark record itself states it - and every mark in every direction is disclosed by its row. Two precision notes, not defects: P06-010 and P06-012 disclose their onset-seam mark as 'parashah evidence' without naming its type. The defects I do raise near the mark layer are A9 placement and A10 framing, which this member does not test.

routed_seam_MT_28_24_28_25: Decided for the corpus, from both faces; no span change to either row. CLOSE FACE (MT 28:24, closing P06-012): the verse ends on the recognition formula with the divine-name pair, which per D3 is refrain-grade close evidence at tier MEASURED and which I confirmed is absent from the inventory's recognition_formula (28) and recognition_formula_2ms (5) lists; pmarks records a SAMEKH after 28:24, and in the C1 direction a mark on a row's last verse stands AT the close seam; pmarks records NO mark after 28:23, so the rival cut has no mark support at all; and MEASURED the verse is Israel-facing from its first words with no second-person form and no reference to Sidon anywhere in it, the 2fs address to Sidon having ended at 28:22. ONSET FACE (MT 28:25, opening P06-013): it is a member of the pinned 122-verse messenger class, and BOTH conditions that license a cut at a messenger formula hold - the addressee changes and a refrain close stands immediately behind it. THE FACT THAT DECIDES THE RIVAL: MT 28:24 appears in NO onset class of the pinned inventory - not the 14 datelines, not word-event 39/41/7, not the 7 hand-of-YHWH verses, not the 122 messenger verses, not the 9 set-your-face verses, not the 93 son-of-man addresses - so a row opening there would open on a verse the book gives no way of opening, and a refrain close does not manufacture an onset. ON THE STRATEGY ENTRY D9 DECLARES WRONG: confirmed independently - the collision shape requires a refrain close followed by a fresh verdict onset, and that shape does not obtain at 28:23/28:24 but does obtain at 28:24/28:25. ON A10: here the tradition's sectioning AGREES with the corpus seam, so it is disclosed corroboration and the text signals decide. Nothing in this seam turns on within-verse mark position, which A8 makes UNAVAILABLE. WHAT MUST STILL CHANGE: P06-012 must withdraw the two sentences placing the addressee turn after 28:24, and P06-013 must replace the MT 33:21-22 precedent with its own measured warrant. Neither is a span change.

P06-007 does it correctly, so the corpus has the pattern.

A measurably false superlative on P07-003, on both faces of the row, on a row both lanes supported and one lane re-asserted.

Both lanes share one grounding error in the same direction on the MT 28:10 emphatic family: LF_c13 says the 14-verse class is 'built on' the kappa-prefixed full form and OL_c13 says the witness carries 'the fuller one in fourteen'. MEASURED by my own sweeps, the kappa-prefixed full form stands on 5 verses and the 14 is the name-bearing form with or without it. Both were right that MT 28:10 is not in the 14 and both were wrong about what the 14 is. This is the clearest case in my group for why correlated agreement is not confirmation, and it is why I re-swept rather than adopting their figure.

A second month-less dateline for D11's arm gap: D11 names MT 32:17 as the dateline naming no month; MEASURED, MT 26:1 has the same shape (year 11 and day 1, no month term). MT 26:1 is in no row of mine, so I file nothing and report it because D11 is a corpus-wide check whose list looks short by one.

A1 is satisfied on both halves for every K/Q my rows quote, which resolves an item OL_c13 left unresolved: every ketiv quoted is present as a running-text token in the OSHB bytes, and every Qere is labelled and slash-free while the note layer carries the slash.

I touched neither file. CONTAINMENT: I re-ran my largest finding, the A6 audit, from a single self-contained script importing no helper, and it reproduced my original result exactly - 1273 WEB verses parsed and 16 runs of five or more words with an identical per-row distribution. My deliverable builder imports no helper either, so no figure I report depends on a file that changed under me. WHY IT MATTERS UPWARD: the hazard is the shared filename, not my result. Two peers importing the same helper name from one directory can each compute against a parser the other wrote, silently and with no error raised - and the two parsers differ precisely in multi-line WEB verse handling, which is the failure mode the launch messages flagged as having already understated one peer's audit. I cannot check any other peer and am forbidden to read their output, so that is UNAVAILABLE to me. The cheap fix is per-peer filenames or a per-peer subdirectory for working files.

limit: One adjudicating lens over two clusters, eleven rows. I am an Anthropic-family model reconciling two Anthropic-family lanes, so where I agree with them I am a third correlated voice and not independent confirmation; I have tried to make the measurement the ground everywhere and to say so when a conclusion rests on the packets instead. My output is candidate-only and non-authorizing: I propose and I do not decide, and nothing I have written changes a row. Specific limits worth weighing against my findings: my A6 counter works on word identity and so cannot tell a quotation from a collocation, which is why I separated the two classes rather than reporting one number; my A4 application depends on my own extraction of which verses a prose field 'argues', which is a judgement a different lens could draw slightly differently; my universals grading rests on A5's seam-dependence axis, which I flag above as itself unsettled at one edge; and three device-class figures I use are EXTRACTED from the pinned inventory rather than swept by me. I did not re-derive the corpus-wide 708/240 split and I do not present my 11-row A4 measurement as a correction to it.
